285	        lifecycle = {}
286	        raw_lifecycle = document.get("lifecycle", {})
287	        if not isinstance(raw_lifecycle, dict):
288	            raise ObjectStoreError("corrupted index: lifecycle is not a map")
289	        for tenant, policy in raw_lifecycle.items():
290	            if not isinstance(tenant, str) or _TENANT_RE.match(tenant) is None:
291	                raise ObjectStoreError("corrupted index: bad lifecycle tenant")
292	            lifecycle[tenant] = self._validate_lifecycle_policy(policy)
293	        access = {}
294	        raw_access = document.get("access", {})
295	        if not isinstance(raw_access, dict):
296	            raise ObjectStoreError("corrupted index: access is not a map")
297	        for tenant, policy in raw_access.items():
298	            if not isinstance(tenant, str) or _TENANT_RE.match(tenant) is None:
299	                raise ObjectStoreError("corrupted index: bad access tenant")
300	            access[tenant] = self._validate_access_policy(policy)
301	        rate_limit = {}
302	        raw_rate_limit = document.get("rate_limit", {})
303	        if not isinstance(raw_rate_limit, dict):
304	            raise ObjectStoreError("corrupted index: rate_limit is not a map")
305	        for tenant, policy in raw_rate_limit.items():
306	            if not isinstance(tenant, str) or _TENANT_RE.match(tenant) is None:
307	                raise ObjectStoreError("corrupted index: bad rate limit tenant")
308	            rate_limit[tenant] = self._validate_rate_limit_policy(policy)
309	        return (objects, timestamps, records, versioning, versions,
310	                retention, quota, lifecycle, access, rate_limit)
311	
312	    def _load_object_map(self, mapping):
313	        objects, timestamps = {}, {}
314	        for key, entry in mapping.items():
315	            if not isinstance(key, str):
316	                raise ObjectStoreError("corrupted index: non-string key")
317	            objects[key], last_modified = self._validate_entry(key, entry)
318	            if last_modified is not None:
319	                timestamps[key] = last_modified
320	        return objects, timestamps
321	
322	    @staticmethod
323	    def _validate_entry(key, entry):
324	        if not isinstance(entry, dict):
325	            raise ObjectStoreError("corrupted index: entry for %r is not an object" % (key,))
326	        sha, size = entry.get("sha256"), entry.get("size")
327	        content_type = entry.get("content_type")
328	        if not _is_sha256(sha):
329	            raise ObjectStoreError("corrupted index: bad sha256 for %r" % (key,))
330	        if isinstance(size, bool) or not isinstance(size, int) or size < 0:
331	            raise ObjectStoreError("corrupted index: bad size for %r" % (key,))
332	        if content_type is not None and not isinstance(content_type, str):
333	            raise ObjectStoreError("corrupted index: bad content_type for %r" % (key,))
334	        last_modified = entry.get("last_modified")
335	        if last_modified is not None:
336	            if not isinstance(last_modified, str):
337	                raise ObjectStoreError(
338	                    "corrupted index: bad last_modified for %r" % (key,))
339	            try:
340	                datetime.fromisoformat(last_modified)
341	            except ValueError:
342	                raise ObjectStoreError(
343	                    "corrupted index: bad last_modified for %r" % (key,))
344	        return ({"sha256": sha, "size": size, "content_type": content_type},
345	                last_modified)
346	
347	    def _validate_version(self, key, entry):
348	        if not isinstance(entry, dict):
349	            raise ObjectStoreError("corrupted index: version for %r is not an object" % (key,))
350	        version_id = entry.get("version_id")
351	        if not isinstance(version_id, str) or _VERSION_ID_RE.match(version_id) is None:
352	            raise ObjectStoreError("corrupted index: bad version_id for %r" % (key,))
353	        created_at = entry.get("created_at")
354	        if not isinstance(created_at, str):
355	            raise ObjectStoreError("corrupted index: bad created_at for %r" % (key,))
356	        base = self._validate_entry(key, entry)[0]
357	        return {"version_id": version_id, "sha256": base["sha256"],
358	                "size": base["size"], "content_type": base["content_type"],
359	                "created_at": created_at}
360	
361	    @staticmethod
362	    def _validate_policy(policy):
363	        if not isinstance(policy, dict):
364	            raise ObjectStoreError("corrupted index: bad retention policy")
365	        loaded = {}
366	        for name in ("max_versions", "max_age_seconds"):
367	            value = policy.get(name)
368	            if value is None:
369	                continue
370	            if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int) or value < 0:
371	                raise ObjectStoreError("corrupted index: bad retention policy")
372	            loaded[name] = value
373	        if not loaded:
374	            raise ObjectStoreError("corrupted index: bad retention policy")
375	        return loaded
376	
377	    @staticmethod
378	    def _validate_quota(policy):
379	        if not isinstance(policy, dict):
380	            raise ObjectStoreError("corrupted index: bad quota policy")
381	        loaded = {}
382	        for name in ("max_bytes", "max_objects"):
383	            value = policy.get(name)
384	            if value is None:
385	                continue
386	            if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int) or value < 0:
387	                raise ObjectStoreError("corrupted index: bad quota policy")
388	            loaded[name] = value
389	        if not loaded:
390	            raise ObjectStoreError("corrupted index: bad quota policy")
391	        return loaded
392	
393	    @staticmethod
394	    def _validate_lifecycle_policy(policy):
395	        if not isinstance(policy, dict):
396	            raise ObjectStoreError("corrupted index: bad lifecycle policy")
397	        prefix = policy.get("prefix", "")
398	        if not isinstance(prefix, str):
399	            raise ObjectStoreError("corrupted index: bad lifecycle policy")
400	        max_age = policy.get("max_age_seconds")
401	        if isinstance(max_age, bool) or not isinstance(max_age, int) or max_age < 0:
402	            raise ObjectStoreError("corrupted index: bad lifecycle policy")
403	        return {"prefix": prefix, "max_age_seconds": max_age}

405	    @staticmethod

528	    @staticmethod
529	    def _check_precondition(expected_sha256):
530	        """Normalize an ``expected_sha256`` keyword argument.
531	
532	        Omitted (the ``_MISSING`` sentinel) means no condition; an explicit
533	        ``None`` means the key must not exist; a 64-digit lowercase hex string
534	        means the key must exist with that exact digest. Anything else is an
535	        ``invalid precondition`` error rather than a failed condition.
536	        """
537	        if expected_sha256 is _MISSING:
538	            return _MISSING
539	        if expected_sha256 is None:
540	            return None
541	        if _is_sha256(expected_sha256):
542	            return expected_sha256
543	        raise ObjectStoreError("invalid precondition")

545	    def _precondition_met(self, tenant, key, expected):
546	        """Return whether *key* in *tenant* currently satisfies *expected*."""
547	        entry = self._objects.get(tenant, {}).get(key)
548	        if expected is None:
549	            return entry is None
550	        return entry is not None and entry["sha256"] == expected

552	    # -- object API ----------------------------------------------------
553	    def put(self, key, payload, content_type=None, expected_sha256=_MISSING,
554	            tenant=DEFAULT_TENANT):
555	        """Store *payload* under *key* in *tenant* and return its metadata.
556	
557	        *expected_sha256* is an atomic precondition on the key's current
558	        digest in the same tenant: omitted leaves the old overwrite
559	        behaviour, an explicit ``None`` requires the key not to exist, and a
560	        64 lowercase hex digest requires the key to exist with exactly that
561	        digest. Content type and other keys are not compared. Objects of
562	        other tenants are never consulted or touched.
563	
564	        When *tenant* has versioning enabled the write also appends an
565	        immutable version to the key's version list, makes it the current
566	        version and includes its ``version_id`` in the returned metadata.
567	
568	        When *tenant* has a quota policy, the write is rejected with
569	        ``ObjectStoreError("quota exceeded")`` before any data lands when
570	        the resulting usage would exceed a saved limit.
571	        """
572	        self._check_tenant(tenant)
573	        self._check_key(key)
574	        if not isinstance(payload, (bytes, bytearray, memoryview)):
575	            raise ObjectStoreError("payload must be bytes")
576	        if content_type is not None and not isinstance(content_type, str):
577	            raise ObjectStoreError("content_type must be a string or None")
578	        expected = self._check_precondition(expected_sha256)
579	        data = bytes(payload)
580	        sha = hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
581	        entry = {"sha256": sha, "size": len(data), "content_type": content_type}
582	        with self._lock:
583	            if expected is not _MISSING and not self._precondition_met(
584	                    tenant, key, expected):
585	                raise ObjectStoreError("precondition failed")
586	            self._rate_limit_check(tenant, len(data))
587	            versioning_on = self._versioning.get(tenant, False)
588	            delta_bytes, delta_objects = self._publish_delta(
589	                tenant, key, entry, versioning_on)
590	            self._enforce_quota(tenant, delta_bytes, delta_objects)
591	            self._store_blob(sha, data)
592	            self._objects.setdefault(tenant, {})[key] = entry
593	            self._timestamps.setdefault(tenant, {})[key] = \
594	                datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
595	            version_id = None
596	            if versioning_on:
597	                version_id = self._append_version(tenant, key, entry)
598	            self._save_index()
599	            result = dict(entry)
600	            if version_id is not None:
601	                result["version_id"] = version_id
602	            return result

604	    def _append_version(self, tenant, key, entry):
605	        """Append a new immutable version for *key* and return its id.
606	
607	        Must be called under the store lock; the caller makes the matching
608	        current-pointer update and saves the index.
609	        """
610	        versions = self._versions.setdefault(tenant, {}).setdefault(key, [])
611	        existing = {version["version_id"] for version in versions}
612	        while True:
613	            version_id = uuid.uuid4().hex
614	            if version_id not in existing:
615	                break
616	        versions.append({
617	            "version_id": version_id,
618	            "sha256": entry["sha256"],
619	            "size": entry["size"],
620	            "content_type": entry["content_type"],
621	            "created_at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
622	        })
623	        return version_id

625	    def _store_blob(self, sha, data):
626	        """Write the blob for *sha* when missing and repair it when corrupted.
627	
628	        An existing file is hashed on every put. Intact files are left exactly
629	        as they are so dedup costs nothing extra; a file whose digest no longer
630	        matches is rewritten atomically from the complete *data*, so an
631	        interrupted repair leaves either the old bytes or the full new bytes.
632	        """
633	        path = os.path.join(self.blobs_dir, sha)
634	        if os.path.exists(path):
635	            try:
636	                with open(path, "rb") as handle:
637	                    stored = handle.read()
638	            except FileNotFoundError:
639	                stored = None
640	            except OSError:
641	                raise ObjectStoreError("blob io error")
642	            if stored is not None:
643	                if hashlib.sha256(stored).hexdigest() == sha:
644	                    return
645	                try:
646	                    _atomic_write(path, data)
647	                except OSError:
648	                    raise ObjectStoreError("blob io error")
649	                return
650	        try:
651	            _atomic_write(path, data)
652	        except OSError:
653	            raise ObjectStoreError("blob io error")

655	    def get(self, key, tenant=DEFAULT_TENANT, expires=None, signature=None):
656	        """Return ``(payload, entry)`` for *key* in *tenant*.
657	
658	        When *tenant* has a signed access policy, *expires* and *signature*
659	        must hold an unexpired signature for the ``GET`` method (see
660	        :meth:`sign_request`); anything else raises
661	        ``ObjectStoreError("access denied")`` before the key is looked up.
662	        """
663	        self._check_tenant(tenant)
664	        self._check_key(key)
665	        with self._lock:
666	            self._check_read_access(tenant, key, None, expires, signature,
667	                                    "GET")
668	            self._rate_limit_check(tenant)
669	            entry = self._head_unlocked(tenant, key)
670	            data = self._blob_unlocked(entry["sha256"])
671	            if len(data) != entry["size"]:
672	                raise ObjectStoreError("corrupted blob")

675	    def head(self, key, tenant=DEFAULT_TENANT, expires=None, signature=None):

678	        Signed tenants require the same ``expires``/``signature`` pair as
679	        :meth:`get`, but computed for the ``HEAD`` method.
680	        """

682	        self._check_key(key)
683	        with self._lock:
684	            self._check_read_access(tenant, key, None, expires, signature,
685	                                    "HEAD")

687	            return self._head_unlocked(tenant, key)

701	    def _head_unlocked(self, tenant, key):

708	    def delete(self, key, expected_sha256=_MISSING, tenant=DEFAULT_TENANT):
709	        """Drop *key* in *tenant*; shared blobs stay on disk for other keys.
710	
711	        With *expected_sha256*, deletion also requires the key's current
712	        digest in this tenant to match (or an explicit ``None`` requires the
713	        key absent); a satisfied absent-condition delete still reports the
714	        key as not found. Objects other tenants keep under the same key are
715	        unaffected.
716	
717	        When *tenant* has versioning enabled and the key has versions, only
718	        the current version is removed: the newest remaining version becomes
719	        current, and the key disappears entirely once no version remains.
720	        """
721	        self._check_tenant(tenant)
722	        self._check_key(key)
723	        expected = self._check_precondition(expected_sha256)
724	        with self._lock:
725	            objects = self._objects.get(tenant, {})
726	            if key not in objects:
727	                raise ObjectStoreError("not found: %s" % (key,))
728	            if expected is not _MISSING and not self._precondition_met(
729	                    tenant, key, expected):
730	                raise ObjectStoreError("precondition failed")
731	            self._rate_limit_check(tenant)
732	            self._remove_current_unlocked(tenant, key)
733	            self._save_index()

735	    def _remove_current_unlocked(self, tenant, key):
736	        """Remove *key*'s current object the way :meth:`delete` does.
737	
738	        Versioned tenants pop the current version and promote the newest
739	        remaining one; unversioned tenants drop the mapping outright. When a
740	        version is promoted its ``created_at`` becomes the key's
741	        last-modified time (that content's last write); when the mapping is
742	        removed the saved timestamp is dropped with it. Must be called under
743	        the store lock with *key* present; returns the removed current entry.
744	        """
745	        objects = self._objects[tenant]
746	        removed = dict(objects[key])
747	        versions = self._versions.get(tenant, {}).get(key)
748	        if self._versioning.get(tenant, False) and versions:
749	            versions.pop()
750	            if versions:
751	                promoted = versions[-1]
752	                objects[key] = {"sha256": promoted["sha256"],
753	                                "size": promoted["size"],
754	                                "content_type": promoted["content_type"]}
755	                self._timestamps.setdefault(tenant, {})[key] = \
756	                    promoted["created_at"]
757	            else:
758	                del objects[key]
759	                self._timestamps.get(tenant, {}).pop(key, None)
760	                self._drop_versions_key(tenant, key)
761	        else:
762	            del objects[key]
763	            self._timestamps.get(tenant, {}).pop(key, None)
764	        return removed
765	
766	    def _drop_versions_key(self, tenant, key):
767	        """Remove *key*'s (empty) version list and prune empty parent maps."""
768	        keymap = self._versions.get(tenant)
769	        if keymap is None:
770	            return
771	        keymap.pop(key, None)
772	        if not keymap:
773	            del self._versions[tenant]

775	    def blob(self, sha256, tenant=DEFAULT_TENANT):
776	        """Return the raw bytes stored under digest *sha256*.
777	
778	        The digest of the bytes actually on disk is recomputed on every read,
779	        so truncation, appended bytes and same-length tampering are all
780	        rejected instead of being handed back to the caller.
781	
782	        Blobs stay global; *tenant* only selects the rate limit policy the
783	        read is accounted against (the default tenant when omitted).
784	        """
785	        self._require_sha(sha256)
786	        self._check_tenant(tenant)
787	        with self._lock:
788	            self._rate_limit_check(tenant)
789	            return self._blob_unlocked(sha256)
790	
791	    def _blob_unlocked(self, sha256):
792	        """Return the verified bytes of *sha256*; must be called under the lock."""
793	        try:
794	            with open(os.path.join(self.blobs_dir, sha256), "rb") as handle:
795	                data = handle.read()
796	        except FileNotFoundError:
797	            raise ObjectStoreError("not found: blob %s" % (sha256,))
798	        except OSError:
799	            raise ObjectStoreError("blob io error")
800	        if hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest() != sha256:
801	            raise ObjectStoreError("corrupted blob")
802	        return data

804	    def blob_digests(self):
805	        """Return the sorted digests currently present in the blob directory."""
806	        with self._lock:
807	            return sorted(name for name in os.listdir(self.blobs_dir) if _is_sha256(name))

816	    def _load_uploads(self):
817	        uploads = {}
818	        try:
819	            names = os.listdir(self.uploads_dir)
820	        except FileNotFoundError:
821	            return uploads
822	        except OSError:
823	            raise ObjectStoreError("upload io error")
824	        for name in sorted(names):
825	            match = _SESSION_META_RE.match(name)
826	            if match is None:
827	                continue
828	            session_id = match.group(1)
829	            if session_id in self._upload_records:
830	                # completed before a crash could clean its files up
831	                self._discard_session_files(session_id)
832	                continue
833	            session = self._read_session_meta(session_id)
834	            self._check_part_file(session_id, session["offset"])

838	    def _read_session_meta(self, session_id):
839	        try:
840	            with open(self._session_meta_path(session_id), "rb") as handle:
841	                document = json.loads(handle.read().decode("utf-8"))
842	        except (OSError, ValueError, UnicodeDecodeError) as exc:
843	            raise ObjectStoreError("corrupted upload session: %s" % (exc,))
844	        if not isinstance(document, dict):
845	            raise ObjectStoreError("corrupted upload session: not an object")
846	        key = document.get("key")
847	        size = document.get("size")
848	        sha = document.get("sha256")
849	        content_type = document.get("content_type")
850	        offset = document.get("offset")
851	        expected = document.get("expected_sha256", _MISSING)
852	        tenant = document.get("tenant", DEFAULT_TENANT)
853	        try:
854	            self._check_key(key)
855	        except ObjectStoreError:
856	            raise ObjectStoreError("corrupted upload session: bad key")
857	        if not isinstance(tenant, str) or _TENANT_RE.match(tenant) is None:
858	            raise ObjectStoreError("corrupted upload session: bad tenant")
859	        if isinstance(size, bool) or not isinstance(size, int) or size < 0:
860	            raise ObjectStoreError("corrupted upload session: bad size")
861	        if not _is_sha256(sha):
862	            raise ObjectStoreError("corrupted upload session: bad sha256")
863	        if content_type is not None and not isinstance(content_type, str):
864	            raise ObjectStoreError("corrupted upload session: bad content_type")
865	        if isinstance(offset, bool) or not isinstance(offset, int) or not 0 <= offset <= size:
866	            raise ObjectStoreError("corrupted upload session: bad offset")
867	        # Sessions written by older versions have no condition; an explicit
868	        # null requires the key absent, a string requires that digest.
869	        if expected is not _MISSING and expected is not None and not _is_sha256(expected):
870	            raise ObjectStoreError("corrupted upload session: bad precondition")
871	        return {"key": key, "size": size, "sha256": sha,
872	                "content_type": content_type, "offset": offset,
873	                "expected_sha256": expected, "tenant": tenant}

875	    def _check_part_file(self, session_id, offset):
876	        """Ensure the part file holds exactly the confirmed *offset* bytes.
877	
878	        A crash between the chunk write and the metadata update can leave
879	        unconfirmed bytes behind; they are truncated so recovery sees either
880	        the old progress or a whole confirmed chunk, never a partial one.
881	        """
882	        path = self._session_part_path(session_id)
883	        try:
884	            size_on_disk = os.stat(path).st_size
885	        except FileNotFoundError:
886	            if offset:
887	                raise ObjectStoreError("corrupted upload session: missing data")
888	            try:
889	                with open(path, "wb"):
890	                    pass
891	            except OSError:
892	                raise ObjectStoreError("upload io error")
893	            return
894	        except OSError:
895	            raise ObjectStoreError("upload io error")
896	        if size_on_disk < offset:
897	            raise ObjectStoreError("corrupted upload session: truncated data")
898	        if size_on_disk > offset:
899	            try:
900	                with open(path, "r+b") as handle:
901	                    handle.truncate(offset)
902	                    handle.flush()
903	                    os.fsync(handle.fileno())
904	            except OSError:
905	                raise ObjectStoreError("upload io error")

907	    def _save_session(self, session_id, session):
908	        # The default tenant is implicit so older session files stay
909	        # byte-identical; every other tenant is recorded explicitly.
910	        document = {name: value for name, value in session.items()
911	                    if value is not _MISSING
912	                    and not (name == "tenant" and value == DEFAULT_TENANT)}
913	        payload = json.dumps(document, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"))
914	        try:
915	            _atomic_write(self._session_meta_path(session_id),
916	                          payload.encode("utf-8") + b"\n")
917	        except OSError:
918	            raise ObjectStoreError("upload io error")

923	                handle.seek(offset)
924	                handle.write(data)
925	                handle.flush()
926	                os.fsync(handle.fileno())
927	        except OSError:
928	            raise ObjectStoreError("upload io error")

933	                handle.seek(offset)

958	    def _tidy_uploads_dir(self):

992	    def begin_upload(self, key, size, sha256, content_type=None,

997	        must be a non-negative integer (booleans excluded) and *sha256* the
998	        64 lowercase hex digits of the full content's digest. Creating a
999	        session changes no object; the session and its progress survive
1000	        reopening the data directory. The session belongs to *tenant* for its
1001	        whole lifetime: every later operation must name the same tenant.
1002

1004	        it is checked once, atomically with the publish, when the session
1005	        completes, never while the session is created or appended to.
1006

1008	        ``max_bytes`` quota for its whole lifetime: when current usage plus
1009	        the reservations of all active sessions (this one included) would
1010	        exceed the limit, no session is created and
1011	        ``ObjectStoreError("quota exceeded")`` is raised.

1019	            raise ObjectStoreError("content_type must be a string or None")

1021	        session = {"key": key, "size": size, "sha256": sha256,
1022	                   "content_type": content_type, "offset": 0,
1023	                   "expected_sha256": expected, "tenant": tenant}
1024	        with self._lock:
1025	            self._rate_limit_check(tenant)
1026	            self._enforce_reservation(tenant, size)
1027	            session_id = self._new_session_id()
1028	            try:
1029	                os.makedirs(self.uploads_dir, exist_ok=True)
1030	                with open(self._session_part_path(session_id), "wb"):
1031	                    pass
1032	            except OSError:
1033	                raise ObjectStoreError("upload io error")

1035	                self._save_session(session_id, session)
1036	            except ObjectStoreError:
1037	                self._discard_session_files(session_id)

1071	    def append_upload(self, session_id, offset, payload, tenant=DEFAULT_TENANT):
1072	        """Append one chunk to *session_id* and return the received length.
1073	
1074	        A new chunk must start exactly at the current end and may not exceed
1075	        the declared total size. A chunk lying fully inside the received
1076	        range succeeds without growing when its bytes are identical to what
1077	        is stored, and fails otherwise; chunks overlapping the end, chunks
1078	        past the end and empty chunks anywhere but at the end all fail.
1079	        """
1080	        self._check_tenant(tenant)
1081	        self._check_session_id(session_id)
1082	        if isinstance(offset, bool) or not isinstance(offset, int) or offset < 0:
1083	            raise ObjectStoreError("invalid offset: %r" % (offset,))
1084	        if not isinstance(payload, (bytes, bytearray, memoryview)):
1085	            raise ObjectStoreError("payload must be bytes")
1086	        data = bytes(payload)
1087	        with self._lock:
1088	            session = self._require_active_session(session_id, tenant)
1089	            self._rate_limit_check(tenant, len(data))
1090	            current = session["offset"]
1091	            if offset > current:
1092	                raise SessionConflict(
1093	                    "append gap: offset %d beyond received %d" % (offset, current))
1094	            if not data:
1095	                if offset != current:
1096	                    raise SessionConflict("empty chunk only at received end")
1097	                return current
1098	            end = offset + len(data)
1099	            if offset < current:
1100	                if end > current:
1101	                    raise SessionConflict("append overlaps received end")
1102	                if self._read_part(session_id, offset, len(data)) != data:
1103	                    raise SessionConflict("append conflicts with received bytes")
1104	                return current
1105	            if end > session["size"]:
1106	                raise SessionConflict("append exceeds declared size")
1107	            self._write_part(session_id, offset, data)
1108	            self._save_session(session_id, dict(session, offset=end))
1109	            session["offset"] = end
1110	            return end

1112	    def complete_upload(self, session_id, tenant=DEFAULT_TENANT):
1113	        """Publish the object once the received content matches the declaration.
1114	
1115	        The total length and the SHA-256 of the full content must match the
1116	        declared values (zero-byte objects included); only then is the
1117	        session's saved precondition checked against the owning tenant's
1118	        object state at publish time and the object published in that
1119	        tenant, all as one indivisible step. A failed precondition raises
1120	        without changing the object, the session's confirmed bytes or any
1121	        blob, so the session can be completed again (or aborted) later.
1122	        A quota policy on the tenant is enforced the same way: the session's
1123	        own reservation is released first, and when the publish would exceed
1124	        a saved limit ``ObjectStoreError("quota exceeded")`` is raised
1125	        without changing anything. Repeating a completed call returns the
1126	        first result without touching the key again, so later writes or
1127	        deletes of the key are never overwritten.
1128	        """
1129	        self._check_tenant(tenant)
1130	        self._check_session_id(session_id)
1131	        with self._lock:
1132	            record = self._upload_records.get(session_id)
1133	            if record is not None:
1134	                if record["tenant"] != tenant:
1135	                    raise ObjectStoreError(
1136	                        "unknown upload session: %r" % (session_id,))
1137	                entry = dict(record["entry"])
1138	                if record.get("version_id") is not None:
1139	                    entry["version_id"] = record["version_id"]
1140	                return entry
1141	            session = self._uploads.get(session_id)
1142	            if session is None or session["tenant"] != tenant:
1143	                raise ObjectStoreError("unknown upload session: %r" % (session_id,))
1144	            if session["offset"] != session["size"]:
1145	                raise SessionConflict(
1146	                    "upload incomplete: %d of %d bytes received"
1147	                    % (session["offset"], session["size"]))
1148	            data = self._read_part(session_id, 0, session["size"])
1149	            if len(data) != session["size"]:
1150	                raise ObjectStoreError("upload io error")
1151	            if hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest() != session["sha256"]:
1152	                raise SessionConflict("upload hash mismatch")
1153	            expected = session.get("expected_sha256", _MISSING)
1154	            if expected is not _MISSING and not self._precondition_met(
1155	                    tenant, session["key"], expected):
1156	                raise ObjectStoreError("precondition failed")
1157	            self._rate_limit_check(tenant)
1158	            entry = {"sha256": session["sha256"], "size": session["size"],
1159	                     "content_type": session["content_type"]}
1160	            # The session's own reservation is lifted before the quota check:
1161	            # its reserved bytes become the used bytes being published.
1162	            versioning_on = self._versioning.get(tenant, False)
1163	            delta_bytes, delta_objects = self._publish_delta(
1164	                tenant, session["key"], entry, versioning_on)
1165	            self._enforce_quota(tenant, delta_bytes, delta_objects,
1166	                                release_session=session)
1167	            self._store_blob(session["sha256"], data)
1168	            objects = self._objects.setdefault(tenant, {})
1169	            timestamps = self._timestamps.setdefault(tenant, {})
1170	            previous = objects.get(session["key"], _MISSING)
1171	            previous_time = timestamps.get(session["key"], _MISSING)
1172	            published_at = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
1173	            objects[session["key"]] = entry
1174	            timestamps[session["key"]] = published_at
1175	            version_id = None
1176	            if versioning_on:
1177	                version_id = self._append_version(tenant, session["key"], entry)
1178	            record = {"key": session["key"], "entry": dict(entry),
1179	                      "tenant": tenant}
1180	            if version_id is not None:
1181	                record["version_id"] = version_id
1182	            self._upload_records[session_id] = record
1183	            try:
1184	                self._save_index()
1185	            except OSError:
1186	                del self._upload_records[session_id]
1187	                if version_id is not None:
1188	                    self._versions[tenant][session["key"]].pop()
1189	                    self._drop_versions_key(tenant, session["key"])
1190	                if previous is _MISSING:
1191	                    del objects[session["key"]]
1192	                else:
1193	                    objects[session["key"]] = previous
1194	                if previous_time is _MISSING:
1195	                    timestamps.pop(session["key"], None)
1196	                else:
1197	                    timestamps[session["key"]] = previous_time
1198	                raise ObjectStoreError("upload io error")
1199	            del self._uploads[session_id]
1200	            self._discard_session_files(session_id)
1201	            result = dict(entry)
1202	            if version_id is not None:
1203	                result["version_id"] = version_id
1204	            return result

1232	    def collect_garbage(self, dry_run=True):
1233	        """Collect unreferenced blobs, previewing by default.
1234	
1235	        Returns ``{"digests": [...], "bytes": <int>, "dry_run": <bool>}``. The
1236	        digests are sorted lexicographically and bytes is the sum of the actual
1237	        file sizes; a dry run reports the candidates without touching storage,
1238	        an actual run reports the files deleted by that call. Only regular
1239	        files directly in the blobs directory whose names are 64 lowercase hex
1240	        digits are eligible: subdirectories, symlinks, temporary files and any
1241	        other names are left untouched, and symlink targets are never opened.
1242	
1243	        References are recomputed from the current object index on every
1244	        call, across every tenant and including digest sharing between keys.
1245	        Blobs referenced by any retained object version or declared by an
1246	        incomplete upload session are live as well. The whole operation runs
1247	        under the store lock, so blobs published
1248	        concurrently stay referenced and candidates that vanished between
1249	        the scan and deletion are skipped rather than counted.
1250	        """
1251	        if not isinstance(dry_run, bool):
1252	            raise ObjectStoreError("invalid dry_run")
1253	        with self._lock:
1254	            referenced = {
1255	                entry["sha256"]
1256	                for objects in self._objects.values()
1257	                for entry in objects.values()
1258	            }
1259	            for keymap in self._versions.values():
1260	                for versions in keymap.values():
1261	                    for version in versions:
1262	                        referenced.add(version["sha256"])
1263	            for session in self._uploads.values():
1264	                referenced.add(session["sha256"])
1265	            try:
1266	                names = os.listdir(self.blobs_dir)
1267	            except OSError:
1268	                raise ObjectStoreError("gc io error")
1269	            candidates = []
1270	            for name in names:
1271	                if not _is_sha256(name) or name in referenced:
1272	                    continue
1273	                path = os.path.join(self.blobs_dir, name)
1274	                try:
1275	                    info = os.lstat(path)
1276	                except FileNotFoundError:
1277	                    continue
1278	                except OSError:
1279	                    raise ObjectStoreError("gc io error")
1280	                if not stat.S_ISREG(info.st_mode):
1281	                    continue
1282	                candidates.append((name, info.st_size))
1283	            candidates.sort(key=lambda item: item[0])
1284	            if dry_run:
1285	                return {
1286	                    "digests": [name for name, _ in candidates],
1287	                    "bytes": sum(size for _, size in candidates),
1288	                    "dry_run": True,
1289	                }
1290	            deleted = []
1291	            freed = 0
1292	            for name, size in candidates:
1293	                path = os.path.join(self.blobs_dir, name)
1294	                try:
1295	                    os.remove(path)
1296	                except FileNotFoundError:
1297	                    continue
1298	                except OSError:
1299	                    raise ObjectStoreError("gc io error")
1300	                deleted.append(name)
1301	                freed += size
1302	            return {"digests": deleted, "bytes": freed, "dry_run": False}

1389	    def list_versions(self, key, after=None, limit=DEFAULT_LIMIT,
1390	                      tenant=DEFAULT_TENANT):
1391	        """Return ``{"items": [...], "next_after": <str|null>}`` for one page.
1392	
1393	        Versions of *key* in *tenant* are listed newest first (creation
1394	        order reversed); each item holds ``version_id``, ``sha256``,
1395	        ``size``, ``created_at`` and a ``current`` flag. *after* is the
1396	        exclusive ``version_id`` cursor handed out as ``next_after`` and
1397	        *limit* follows the same rules as :meth:`list_objects`. Requires
1398	        versioning to be enabled for the tenant.
1399	        """
1400	        self._check_tenant(tenant)
1401	        self._check_key(key)
1402	        if after is not None and not isinstance(after, str):
1403	            raise ObjectStoreError("invalid version")
1404	        limit = self._check_limit(limit)
1405	        with self._lock:
1406	            self._rate_limit_check(tenant)
1407	            self._require_versioning(tenant)
1408	            versions = self._versions_of(tenant, key)
1409	            current_id = versions[-1]["version_id"]
1410	            ordered = list(reversed(versions))
1411	            if after is not None:
1412	                position = next(
1413	                    (index for index, version in enumerate(ordered)
1414	                     if version["version_id"] == after), None)
1415	                if position is None:
1416	                    raise ObjectStoreError("invalid version")
1417	                ordered = ordered[position + 1:]
1418	            page = ordered[:limit]
1419	            items = [self._version_item(version, current_id) for version in page]
1420	            return {"items": items,
1421	                    "next_after": page[-1]["version_id"]
1422	                    if len(ordered) > len(page) else None}

# -- retention -------------------------------------------------------
    def set_retention(self, max_versions=None, max_age_seconds=None,
                      tenant=DEFAULT_TENANT):
        """Save the retention policy of *tenant*.

        At least one of *max_versions* and *max_age_seconds* must be
        given, and each given value must be a non-negative integer
        (booleans excluded); anything else raises
        ``ObjectStoreError("invalid retention")``. The policy only takes
        effect through :meth:`purge_retention`.
        """
        self._check_tenant(tenant)
        for value in (max_versions, max_age_seconds):
            if value is not None and (isinstance(value, bool)
                                      or not isinstance(value, int)
                                      or value < 0):
                raise ObjectStoreError("invalid retention")
        if max_versions is None and max_age_seconds is None:
            raise ObjectStoreError("invalid retention")
        policy = {}
        if max_versions is not None:
            policy["max_versions"] = max_versions
        if max_age_seconds is not None:
            policy["max_age_seconds"] = max_age_seconds
        with self._lock:
            self._rate_limit_check(tenant)
            self._retention[tenant] = policy
            self._save_index()

    def get_retention(self, tenant=DEFAULT_TENANT):
        """Return *tenant*'s retention policy, or None when none is saved.

        A saved policy is returned as a dict with both ``max_versions``
        and ``max_age_seconds`` keys, unset limits reading as None.
        """
        self._check_tenant(tenant)
        with self._lock:
            self._rate_limit_check(tenant)
            policy = self._retention.get(tenant)
            if policy is None:
                return None
            return {"max_versions": policy.get("max_versions"),
                    "max_age_seconds": policy.get("max_age_seconds")}

    def purge_retention(self, dry_run=True, tenant=DEFAULT_TENANT):
        """Apply *tenant*'s saved retention policy to its object versions.

        Returns ``{"versions": [...], "bytes": <int>, "dry_run": <bool>}``
        where the versions are the entries the policy removes (or would
        remove), sorted by ``version_id``, and bytes is the sum of their
        sizes. The current version of every key is always kept; of the
        remaining versions, any beyond the newest ``max_versions`` per key
        or older than ``max_age_seconds`` (compared against the current
        UTC time) are removed. A dry run changes nothing. Without a saved
        policy the result is empty.
        """
        self._check_tenant(tenant)
        if not isinstance(dry_run, bool):
            raise ObjectStoreError("invalid dry_run")
        with self._lock:
            self._rate_limit_check(tenant)
            policy = self._retention.get(tenant)
            if policy is None:
                return {"versions": [], "bytes": 0, "dry_run": dry_run}
            max_versions = policy.get("max_versions")
            max_age = policy.get("max_age_seconds")
            now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
            keymap = self._versions.get(tenant, {})
            plan = {}
            purged = []
            for key in sorted(keymap):
                versions = keymap[key]
                if not versions:
                    continue
                remove = set()
                if max_versions is not None:
                    keep = max(1, max_versions)
                    for version in versions[:-keep]:
                        remove.add(version["version_id"])
                if max_age is not None:
                    cutoff = now - timedelta(seconds=max_age)
                    for version in versions[:-1]:
                        try:
                            created = datetime.fromisoformat(
                                version["created_at"])
                        except ValueError:
                            continue
                        if created < cutoff:
                            remove.add(version["version_id"])
                if not remove:
                    continue
                plan[key] = remove
                for version in versions:
                    if version["version_id"] in remove:
                        purged.append({"key": key,
                                       "version_id": version["version_id"],
                                       "sha256": version["sha256"],
                                       "size": version["size"],
                                       "created_at": version["created_at"]})
            purged.sort(key=lambda item: item["version_id"])
            result = {"versions": purged,
                      "bytes": sum(item["size"] for item in purged),
                      "dry_run": dry_run}
            if dry_run or not plan:
                return result
            saved = {key: list(versions) for key, versions in keymap.items()}
            for key, remove in plan.items():
                remaining = [version for version in keymap[key]
                             if version["version_id"] not in remove]
                if remaining:
                    keymap[key] = remaining
                else:
                    self._drop_versions_key(tenant, key)
            if tenant in self._versions and not self._versions[tenant]:
                del self._versions[tenant]
            try:
                self._save_index()
            except OSError:
                if saved:
                    self._versions[tenant] = saved
                else:
                    self._versions.pop(tenant, None)
                raise ObjectStoreError("version io error")
            return result

    # -- quota and usage -------------------------------------------------
    @staticmethod
    def _key_usage(entry, versions):
        """Return the logical (bytes, objects) one key contributes.

        Every retained version counts once; the current object entry counts
        only when it is not a pointer at the newest version's content, so a
        versioned key is never double-counted while an unversioned overwrite
        of a formerly versioned key still counts both the retained history
        and the diverging current object.
        """
        total_bytes = 0
        total_objects = 0
        for version in versions or ():
            total_bytes += version["size"]
            total_objects += 1
        if entry is not None and not (
                versions and versions[-1]["sha256"] == entry["sha256"]):
            total_bytes += entry["size"]
            total_objects += 1
        return total_bytes, total_objects

    def _usage_unlocked(self, tenant):
        """Return *tenant*'s current usage; must be called under the lock."""
        objects = self._objects.get(tenant, {})
        keymap = self._versions.get(tenant, {})
        used_bytes = 0
        used_objects = 0
        for key in set(objects) | set(keymap):
            delta_bytes, delta_objects = self._key_usage(
                objects.get(key), keymap.get(key) or None)
            used_bytes += delta_bytes
            used_objects += delta_objects
        reserved_bytes = 0
        reserved_sessions = 0
        for session in self._uploads.values():
            if session["tenant"] == tenant:
                reserved_bytes += session["size"]
                reserved_sessions += 1
        return {"used_bytes": used_bytes, "used_objects": used_objects,
                "reserved_bytes": reserved_bytes,
                "reserved_sessions": reserved_sessions}

    def _publish_delta(self, tenant, key, entry, versioning_on):
        """Return the (bytes, objects) *tenant* gains when *entry* is published.

        Must be called under the store lock, before the mutation happens.
        """
        objects = self._objects.get(tenant, {})
        versions = self._versions.get(tenant, {}).get(key) or None
        old_bytes, old_objects = self._key_usage(objects.get(key), versions)
        if versioning_on:
            new_versions = list(versions or ()) + [
                {"sha256": entry["sha256"], "size": entry["size"]}]
        else:
            new_versions = versions
        new_bytes, new_objects = self._key_usage(entry, new_versions)
        return new_bytes - old_bytes, new_objects - old_objects

    def _enforce_quota(self, tenant, delta_bytes, delta_objects,
                       release_session=None):
        """Raise ``quota exceeded`` when the delta would break *tenant*'s quota.

        Byte limits apply to used plus reserved space. *release_session* is
        an active upload session whose own reservation is lifted before the
        check, because completing it turns those reserved bytes into the used
        bytes being accounted here. Must be called under the store lock.
        """
        policy = self._quota.get(tenant)
        if not policy:
            return
        usage = self._usage_unlocked(tenant)
        reserved = usage["reserved_bytes"]
        if release_session is not None:
            reserved -= release_session["size"]
        max_bytes = policy.get("max_bytes")
        if max_bytes is not None and \
                usage["used_bytes"] + reserved + delta_bytes > max_bytes:
            raise ObjectStoreError("quota exceeded")
        max_objects = policy.get("max_objects")
        if max_objects is not None and \
                usage["used_objects"] + delta_objects > max_objects:
            raise ObjectStoreError("quota exceeded")

    def _enforce_reservation(self, tenant, size):
        """Raise ``quota exceeded`` when reserving *size* more bytes breaks quota."""
        policy = self._quota.get(tenant)
        if not policy:
            return
        max_bytes = policy.get("max_bytes")
        if max_bytes is None:
            return
        usage = self._usage_unlocked(tenant)
        if usage["used_bytes"] + usage["reserved_bytes"] + size > max_bytes:
            raise ObjectStoreError("quota exceeded")

    def set_quota(self, max_bytes=None, max_objects=None, tenant=DEFAULT_TENANT):
        """Save the quota policy of *tenant*.

        At least one of *max_bytes* and *max_objects* must be given, and
        each given value must be a non-negative integer (booleans excluded);
        anything else raises ``ObjectStoreError("invalid quota")``. The
        policy is persisted with the index; an I/O failure while saving
        raises ``ObjectStoreError("quota io error")`` and keeps the previous
        policy. *max_bytes* limits used plus reserved bytes, *max_objects*
        the number of logical objects (current objects plus retained
        versions).
        """
        self._check_tenant(tenant)
        for value in (max_bytes, max_objects):
            if value is not None and (isinstance(value, bool)
                                      or not isinstance(value, int)
                                      or value < 0):
                raise ObjectStoreError("invalid quota")
        if max_bytes is None and max_objects is None:
            raise ObjectStoreError("invalid quota")
        policy = {}
        if max_bytes is not None:
            policy["max_bytes"] = max_bytes
        if max_objects is not None:
            policy["max_objects"] = max_objects
        with self._lock:
            self._rate_limit_check(tenant)
            previous = self._quota.get(tenant)
            self._quota[tenant] = policy
            try:
                self._save_index()
            except OSError:
                if previous is None:
                    del self._quota[tenant]
                else:
                    self._quota[tenant] = previous
                raise ObjectStoreError("quota io error")

    def get_quota(self, tenant=DEFAULT_TENANT):
        """Return *tenant*'s quota policy, or None when none is saved.

        A saved policy is returned as a dict with both ``max_bytes`` and
        ``max_objects`` keys, unset limits reading as None.
        """
        self._check_tenant(tenant)
        with self._lock:
            self._rate_limit_check(tenant)
            policy = self._quota.get(tenant)
            if policy is None:
                return None
            return {"max_bytes": policy.get("max_bytes"),
                    "max_objects": policy.get("max_objects")}

    def clear_quota(self, tenant=DEFAULT_TENANT):
        """Drop *tenant*'s quota policy and return None; the tenant is unlimited.

        Clearing a tenant without a policy is a no-op. An I/O failure while
        saving raises ``ObjectStoreError("quota io error")`` and keeps the
        previous policy.
        """
        self._check_tenant(tenant)
        with self._lock:
            self._rate_limit_check(tenant)
            previous = self._quota.pop(tenant, None)
            try:
                self._save_index()
            except OSError:
                if previous is not None:
                    self._quota[tenant] = previous
                raise ObjectStoreError("quota io error")

    def get_usage(self, tenant=DEFAULT_TENANT):
        """Return *tenant*'s current usage as four integer counters.

        ``used_bytes``/``used_objects`` count logical references: every
        current object and every retained version once (a current pointer
        duplicating its newest version is not counted twice, and keys
        sharing a digest count separately). ``reserved_bytes``/
        ``reserved_sessions`` count the declared sizes of the tenant's
        active upload sessions, released on completion or abort.
        """
        self._check_tenant(tenant)
        with self._lock:
            self._rate_limit_check(tenant)
            return self._usage_unlocked(tenant)

    # -- lifecycle -------------------------------------------------------
    def set_lifecycle(self, max_age_seconds, prefix="", tenant=DEFAULT_TENANT):
        """Save *tenant*'s lifecycle expiration policy.

        *prefix* must be a string (empty when omitted) and
        *max_age_seconds* a required non-negative integer (booleans
        excluded); a missing age or any other value raises
        ``ObjectStoreError("invalid lifecycle")``. The policy only takes
        effect through :meth:`run_lifecycle` and is persisted atomically
        with the index, an I/O failure raising
        ``ObjectStoreError("lifecycle io error")`` and keeping the previous
        policy.
        """
        self._check_tenant(tenant)
        policy = self._check_lifecycle_values(prefix, max_age_seconds)
        with self._lock:
            self._rate_limit_check(tenant)
            previous = self._lifecycle.get(tenant)
            self._lifecycle[tenant] = policy
            try:
                self._save_index()
            except OSError:
                if previous is None:
                    del self._lifecycle[tenant]
                else:
                    self._lifecycle[tenant] = previous
                raise ObjectStoreError("lifecycle io error")

    @staticmethod
    def _check_lifecycle_values(prefix, max_age_seconds):
        if not isinstance(prefix, str):
            raise ObjectStoreError("invalid lifecycle")
        if isinstance(max_age_seconds, bool) \
                or not isinstance(max_age_seconds, int) \
                or max_age_seconds < 0:
            raise ObjectStoreError("invalid lifecycle")
        return {"prefix": prefix, "max_age_seconds": max_age_seconds}

    def get_lifecycle(self, tenant=DEFAULT_TENANT):
        """Return *tenant*'s lifecycle policy, or None when none is saved."""
        self._check_tenant(tenant)
        with self._lock:
            self._rate_limit_check(tenant)
            policy = self._lifecycle.get(tenant)
            if policy is None:
                return None
            return {"prefix": policy["prefix"],
                    "max_age_seconds": policy["max_age_seconds"]}

    def clear_lifecycle(self, tenant=DEFAULT_TENANT):
        """Drop *tenant*'s lifecycle policy and return None.

        Clearing a tenant without a policy is a no-op. An I/O failure while
        saving raises ``ObjectStoreError("lifecycle io error")`` and keeps
        the previous policy.
        """
        self._check_tenant(tenant)
        with self._lock:
            self._rate_limit_check(tenant)
            previous = self._lifecycle.pop(tenant, None)
            try:
                self._save_index()
            except OSError:
                if previous is not None:
                    self._lifecycle[tenant] = previous
                raise ObjectStoreError("lifecycle io error")

    @staticmethod
    def _parse_timestamp(value):
        """Parse an ISO UTC timestamp; a naive value is assumed to be UTC."""
        parsed = datetime.fromisoformat(value)
        if parsed.tzinfo is None:
            return parsed.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
        return parsed

    def run_lifecycle(self, dry_run=True, tenant=DEFAULT_TENANT):
        """Preview or delete *tenant*'s expired current objects.

        Returns ``{"objects": [...], "bytes": <int>, "dry_run": <bool>}``.
        The cutoff is the current UTC time minus the policy's
        ``max_age_seconds``; only the tenant's current objects whose keys
        start with the policy ``prefix`` and whose last-modified time is
        older than the cutoff are candidates, sorted by key. Objects whose
        index entry has no last-modified time (objects first written by an
        older version) are timeless and always skipped. Each result entry
        holds ``key``, ``sha256`` and ``size`` and bytes is the sum of
        their sizes. Without a saved policy the result is empty. A dry run
        (the default) changes nothing; an actual run performs every removal
        under the store lock in one atomic index rewrite, following
        :meth:`delete`'s current-version removal and old-version promotion
        rules for versioned tenants and simply dropping the mapping for
        unversioned ones. Active upload sessions are never touched, and
        only metadata references are removed: the blob bytes stay for
        :meth:`collect_garbage`. An I/O failure restores every object map,
        version list and (derived) quota counter and raises
        ``ObjectStoreError("lifecycle io error")``.
        """
        self._check_tenant(tenant)
        if not isinstance(dry_run, bool):
            raise ObjectStoreError("invalid dry_run")
        with self._lock:
            self._rate_limit_check(tenant)
            policy = self._lifecycle.get(tenant)
            if policy is None:
                return {"objects": [], "bytes": 0, "dry_run": dry_run}
            prefix = policy["prefix"]
            cutoff = datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta(
                seconds=policy["max_age_seconds"])
            objects = self._objects.get(tenant, {})
            timestamps = self._timestamps.get(tenant, {})
            candidates = []
            for key in sorted(objects):
                if not key.startswith(prefix):
                    continue
                last_modified = timestamps.get(key)
                if last_modified is None:
                    continue
                if self._parse_timestamp(last_modified) < cutoff:
                    entry = objects[key]
                    candidates.append({
                        "key": key,
                        "sha256": entry["sha256"],
                        "size": entry["size"],
                    })
            result = {"objects": candidates,
                      "bytes": sum(item["size"] for item in candidates),
                      "dry_run": dry_run}
            if dry_run or not candidates:
                return result
            saved_objects = {name: dict(mapping)
                             for name, mapping in self._objects.items()}
            saved_timestamps = {name: dict(mapping)
                                for name, mapping in self._timestamps.items()}
            saved_versions = {
                name: {key: list(versions)
                       for key, versions in keymap.items()}
                for name, keymap in self._versions.items()}
            try:
                for item in candidates:
                    self._remove_current_unlocked(tenant, item["key"])
                self._save_index()
            except OSError:
                self._objects = saved_objects
                self._timestamps = saved_timestamps
                self._versions = saved_versions
                raise ObjectStoreError("lifecycle io error")
            return result

    # -- access policy and read signatures -------------------------------
    @staticmethod
    def _access_signature(secret, tenant, method, key, version_id, expires):
        """Return the HMAC-SHA256 hex digest signing one read request."""
        payload = "\n".join((tenant, method, key,
                             version_id if version_id is not None else "",
                             str(expires)))
        return hmac.new(secret.encode("utf-8"), payload.encode("utf-8"),
                        hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()

    def get_access_policy(self, tenant=DEFAULT_TENANT):
        """Return *tenant*'s read access policy.

        The result is ``{"mode": "public"}`` when no policy is saved (the
        default, and the state every index written by an older version is
        in) or ``{"mode": "signed", "secret": <str>}`` for a signed tenant.
        """
        self._check_tenant(tenant)
        with self._lock:
            self._rate_limit_check(tenant)
            policy = self._access.get(tenant)
            if policy is None:
                return {"mode": "public"}
            return {"mode": "signed", "secret": policy["secret"]}

    def set_access_policy(self, mode, secret=None, tenant=DEFAULT_TENANT):
        """Save *tenant*'s read access policy.

        *mode* must be ``"public"`` or ``"signed"``; a signed policy
        requires *secret* to be a 16 to 256 character UTF-8 string. Any
        other input raises ``ObjectStoreError("invalid access policy")``.
        Setting ``"public"`` is equivalent to :meth:`clear_access_policy`.
        The policy is persisted atomically with the index; an I/O failure
        while saving raises ``ObjectStoreError("access policy io error")``
        and keeps the previous policy.
        """
        self._check_tenant(tenant)
        if mode == "public":
            self.clear_access_policy(tenant=tenant)
            return
        if mode != "signed":
            raise ObjectStoreError("invalid access policy")
        secret = self._check_secret(secret, "invalid access policy")
        with self._lock:
            self._rate_limit_check(tenant)
            previous = self._access.get(tenant, _MISSING)
            self._access[tenant] = {"mode": "signed", "secret": secret}
            try:
                self._save_index()
            except OSError:
                if previous is _MISSING:
                    del self._access[tenant]
                else:
                    self._access[tenant] = previous
                raise ObjectStoreError("access policy io error")

    def clear_access_policy(self, tenant=DEFAULT_TENANT):
        """Drop *tenant*'s access policy, restoring public reads.

        Clearing a tenant without a policy is a no-op. An I/O failure
        while saving raises ``ObjectStoreError("access policy io error")``
        and keeps the previous policy.
        """
        self._check_tenant(tenant)
        with self._lock:
            self._rate_limit_check(tenant)
            previous = self._access.pop(tenant, None)
            try:
                self._save_index()
            except OSError:
                if previous is not None:
                    self._access[tenant] = previous
                raise ObjectStoreError("access policy io error")

    def sign_request(self, method, key, version_id=None, expires=None,
                     tenant=DEFAULT_TENANT):
        """Sign a read request for *key* in *tenant* and return the hex digest.

        The signed payload is the tenant name, HTTP *method*, object
        *key*, *version_id* (empty when None) and *expires*, joined by
        newlines and hashed with HMAC-SHA256 keyed by the tenant's saved
        secret. *method* must be ``"GET"`` or ``"HEAD"`` and *expires* a
        future integer Unix timestamp; anything else -- or a tenant
        without a signed policy -- raises
        ``ObjectStoreError("invalid signature")``.
        """
        self._check_tenant(tenant)
        self._check_key(key)
        if method not in ("GET", "HEAD"):
            raise ObjectStoreError("invalid signature")
        if version_id is not None and not isinstance(version_id, str):
            raise ObjectStoreError("invalid signature")
        if isinstance(expires, bool) or not isinstance(expires, int) \
                or expires <= time.time():
            raise ObjectStoreError("invalid signature")
        with self._lock:
            policy = self._access.get(tenant)
            if policy is None:
                raise ObjectStoreError("invalid signature")
            return self._access_signature(policy["secret"], tenant, method,
                                          key, version_id, expires)

    def _check_read_access(self, tenant, key, version_id, expires, signature,
                           method):
        """Enforce *tenant*'s read policy; must be called under the lock.

        Public tenants (no saved policy) read freely. Signed tenants must
        present a future integer *expires* and the 64 lowercase hex digits
        of the matching signature, compared in constant time; every other
        input is ``ObjectStoreError("access denied")``, raised before any
        key or version is looked up.
        """
        policy = self._access.get(tenant)
        if policy is None:
            return
        if version_id is not None and not isinstance(version_id, str):
            raise ObjectStoreError("access denied")
        if isinstance(expires, bool) or not isinstance(expires, int) \
                or expires <= time.time():
            raise ObjectStoreError("access denied")
        if not _is_sha256(signature):
            raise ObjectStoreError("access denied")
        expected = self._access_signature(policy["secret"], tenant, method,
                                          key, version_id, expires)
        if not hmac.compare_digest(signature, expected):
            raise ObjectStoreError("access denied")

    def _access_mode(self, tenant):
        """Return ``"public"``/``"signed"`` without rate-limit accounting.

        Used internally by front ends that need the mode to prepare a
        request; the request itself is accounted by the operation it ends
        up calling.
        """
        with self._lock:
            return "signed" if self._access.get(tenant) is not None else "public"

    # -- rate limiting ---------------------------------------------------
    def _rate_limit_check(self, tenant, body_bytes=0):
        """Admit and account one request against *tenant*'s rate limit.

        Must be called under the store lock, after tenant, framing,
        signature and precondition validation and before any state change
        or response. The window is fixed and aligned to the Unix epoch:
        counters reset whenever the window changes. A permitted request is
        accounted immediately (one request plus *body_bytes* against
        ``max_bytes``); a rejected one raises :class:`RateLimitExceeded`
        without touching storage or the counters. Tenants without a saved
        policy are unlimited.
        """
        policy = self._rate_limit.get(tenant)
        if policy is None:
            return
        now = int(time.time())
        window = policy["window_seconds"]
        window_start = (now // window) * window
        state = self._rate_windows.get(tenant)
        if state is None or state["window_start"] != window_start:
            state = self._rate_windows[tenant] = {
                "window_start": window_start, "requests": 0, "bytes": 0}
        max_requests = policy.get("max_requests")
        max_bytes = policy.get("max_bytes")
        if max_requests is not None and state["requests"] + 1 > max_requests \
                or max_bytes is not None and state["bytes"] + body_bytes > max_bytes:
            raise RateLimitExceeded(window_start + window - now)
        state["requests"] += 1
        state["bytes"] += body_bytes

    def set_rate_limit(self, window_seconds, max_requests=None, max_bytes=None,
                       tenant=DEFAULT_TENANT):
        """Save *tenant*'s rate limit policy.

        *window_seconds* is required and must be an integer between 1 and
        86400 (booleans excluded); at least one of *max_requests* and
        *max_bytes* must be given as a non-negative integer (booleans
        excluded). Anything else raises ``ObjectStoreError("invalid rate
        limit")``. The policy is persisted with the index; an I/O failure
        while saving raises ``ObjectStoreError("rate limit io error")``
        and keeps the previous policy. The counters of the current window
        are kept; a window switch always resets them.
        """
        self._check_tenant(tenant)
        if isinstance(window_seconds, bool) \
                or not isinstance(window_seconds, int) \
                or not 1 <= window_seconds <= 86400:
            raise ObjectStoreError("invalid rate limit")
        for value in (max_requests, max_bytes):
            if value is not None and (isinstance(value, bool)
                                      or not isinstance(value, int)
                                      or value < 0):
                raise ObjectStoreError("invalid rate limit")
        if max_requests is None and max_bytes is None:
            raise ObjectStoreError("invalid rate limit")
        policy = {"window_seconds": window_seconds}
        if max_requests is not None:
            policy["max_requests"] = max_requests
        if max_bytes is not None:
            policy["max_bytes"] = max_bytes
        with self._lock:
            previous = self._rate_limit.get(tenant)
            self._rate_limit[tenant] = policy
            try:
                self._save_index()
            except OSError:
                if previous is None:
                    del self._rate_limit[tenant]
                else:
                    self._rate_limit[tenant] = previous
                raise ObjectStoreError("rate limit io error")

    def get_rate_limit(self, tenant=DEFAULT_TENANT):
        """Return *tenant*'s rate limit policy, or None when none is saved.

        A saved policy is returned as a dict with ``window_seconds``,
        ``max_requests`` and ``max_bytes`` keys, unset limits reading as
        None.
        """
        self._check_tenant(tenant)
        with self._lock:
            policy = self._rate_limit.get(tenant)
            if policy is None:
                return None
            return {"window_seconds": policy["window_seconds"],
                    "max_requests": policy.get("max_requests"),
                    "max_bytes": policy.get("max_bytes")}

    def clear_rate_limit(self, tenant=DEFAULT_TENANT):
        """Drop *tenant*'s rate limit policy and return None.

        Clearing a tenant without a policy is a no-op. An I/O failure
        while saving raises ``ObjectStoreError("rate limit io error")``
        and keeps the previous policy.
        """
        self._check_tenant(tenant)
        with self._lock:
            previous = self._rate_limit.pop(tenant, None)
            try:
                self._save_index()
            except OSError:
                if previous is not None:
                    self._rate_limit[tenant] = previous
                raise ObjectStoreError("rate limit io error")

    def get_rate_limit_usage(self, tenant=DEFAULT_TENANT):
        """Return *tenant*'s current-window counters, or None without a policy.

        The result holds ``window_start`` and ``reset_at`` (integer Unix
        seconds bounding the current fixed window) plus the ``requests``
        and ``bytes`` accounted so far in it. Counters live in memory
        only: after a restart they start at zero for the current window.
        """
        self._check_tenant(tenant)
        with self._lock:
            policy = self._rate_limit.get(tenant)
            if policy is None:
                return None
            now = int(time.time())
            window = policy["window_seconds"]
            window_start = (now // window) * window
            state = self._rate_windows.get(tenant)
            requests = bytes_used = 0
            if state is not None and state["window_start"] == window_start:
                requests = state["requests"]
                bytes_used = state["bytes"]
            return {"window_start": window_start,
                    "reset_at": window_start + window,
                    "requests": requests,
                    "bytes": bytes_used}

9	endpoints stay global and ignore it. The versioning and retention endpoints
10	(``/v1/versioning``, ``/v1/objects/{key}/versions[...]``, ``/v1/retention``
11	and ``/v1/retention/purge``), the quota endpoints (``/v1/quota`` and
12	``/v1/usage``), the lifecycle endpoints (``/v1/lifecycle`` and
13	``/v1/lifecycle/run``) and the access-policy endpoint
14	(``/v1/access-policy``) are tenant-scoped the same way.
15	
16	While a tenant's access policy is ``signed``, object and version GET/HEAD
17	requests must carry ``expires`` and ``signature`` query parameters holding

19	expired or mismatching parameters are a 403, while a valid signature on an
20	unknown key or version still gets the plain 404.

23	are tenant-scoped the same way and manage the tenant's fixed-window

25	Every other request is admitted atomically against the selected tenant's

27	a rejected request gets ``429 {"error":"rate limit exceeded"}`` with a

289	    @staticmethod
290	    def _split_version_tail(tail):
291	        """Split ``{key}/versions[/{version_id}]`` tails from plain keys.
292	
293	        Returns ``(key, version_id, is_version_path)``; a plain object key
294	        comes back unchanged with ``is_version_path`` false.
295	        """
296	        marker = "/versions"
297	        if tail.endswith(marker) and len(tail) > len(marker):
298	            return tail[:-len(marker)], None, True
299	        marker += "/"
300	        if marker in tail:
301	            key, _, version_id = tail.rpartition(marker)
302	            if key and version_id and "/" not in version_id:
303	                return key, version_id, True
304	        return tail, None, False

306	    def _object(self, method, tail, query=""):
307	        tenant = self._tenant()
308	        if not tail:
309	            return self._error(400, "invalid key")
310	        key, version_id, is_version_path = self._split_version_tail(tail)
311	        if is_version_path:
312	            if version_id is None:
313	                if method != "GET":
314	                    return self._error(405, "method not allowed")
315	                return self._list_versions(key, query, tenant)
316	            return self._version_item(method, key, version_id, tenant, query)
317	        store = self.server.store
318	        if method == "PUT":
319	            body = self._read_body()
320	            if body is None:
321	                return self._error(411, "length required")
322	            ContentAddressedStore._check_key(key)
323	            expected = self._precondition_headers()
324	            try:
325	                # Peek without accounting: the PUT itself is the request
326	                # that counts, so the pre-write existence check must not
327	                # consume the tenant's rate limit budget.
328	                existing = store._peek_head(tenant, key)
329	            except ObjectStoreError:
330	                existing = None
331	            entry = store.put(key, body, content_type=self.headers.get("Content-Type"),
332	                              expected_sha256=expected, tenant=tenant)
333	            repeated = existing is not None and existing["sha256"] == entry["sha256"]
334	            body_out = {"key": key, "sha256": entry["sha256"], "size": entry["size"]}
335	            if "version_id" in entry:
336	                body_out["version_id"] = entry["version_id"]
337	            return self._send(200 if repeated else 201, _json_bytes(body_out))
338	        if method == "GET":
339	            data, entry = store.get(key, tenant=tenant,
340	                                    **self._access_params(query, tenant))
341	            return self._send(200, data, entry["content_type"] or _DEFAULT_CONTENT_TYPE,
342	                              self._etag_headers(entry))
343	        if method == "HEAD":
344	            entry = store.head(key, tenant=tenant,
345	                               **self._access_params(query, tenant))
346	            return self._send(200, b"", entry["content_type"] or _DEFAULT_CONTENT_TYPE,
347	                              self._etag_headers(entry), head_only=True,
348	                              length=entry["size"])
349	        if method == "DELETE":
350	            ContentAddressedStore._check_key(key)
351	            expected = self._precondition_headers()
352	            store.delete(key, expected_sha256=expected, tenant=tenant)
353	            return self._send(204, b"")
354	        return self._error(405, "method not allowed")

356	    # -- resumable upload sessions -------------------------------------
357	    def _read_length_body(self):
358	        """Read a body framed strictly by Content-Length.
359	
360	        Transfer-Encoding wins over every other problem (400); a missing,
361	        non-integer or negative Content-Length is 411; a body that ends
362	        before the declared length is 400. Returns ``(body, (status,
363	        message))`` with the error element ``None`` on success.
364	        """
365	        if self.headers.get("Transfer-Encoding") is not None:
366	            self.close_connection = True
367	            return None, (400, "transfer encoding not supported")
368	        raw = self.headers.get("Content-Length")
369	        if raw is None or _DECIMAL_RE.match(raw) is None:
370	            self.close_connection = True
371	            return None, (411, "length required")
372	        length = int(raw)
373	        body = self.rfile.read(length) if length else b""
374	        if len(body) != length:
375	            self.close_connection = True
376	            return None, (400, "truncated request body")
377	        return body, None

379	    @staticmethod
380	    def _json_object(body):
381	        """Decode *body* as a UTF-8 JSON object or raise a 400-class error."""
382	        try:
383	            text = body.decode("utf-8")
384	        except UnicodeDecodeError:
385	            raise ObjectStoreError("invalid json: body is not utf-8")
386	        try:
387	            document = json.loads(text)
388	        except ValueError:
389	            raise ObjectStoreError("invalid json: body is not a json document")
390	        if not isinstance(document, dict):
391	            raise ObjectStoreError("invalid json: body must be a json object")
392	        return document

394	    @staticmethod
395	    def _offset_param(query):
396	        """Return the unique non-negative decimal ``offset`` query value."""
397	        params = parse_qs(query, keep_blank_values=True)
398	        values = params.get("offset")
399	        if values is None or len(values) != 1 or _DECIMAL_RE.match(values[0]) is None:
400	            raise ObjectStoreError("invalid offset")
401	        return int(values[0])
